content:
incident-bot: ALERT: slo_burn_rate for service=redwood-inference route=/v1/generate crossed threshold. windows: 5m=4.2x, 1h=1.1x, 6h=1.0x. paging policy=page-on-high. Incident created: INC-2023-8492. Details: https://grafana.internal/r/alerts/8492
Maya (oncall): taking this — I'm paged. Anyone on deck for quick mitigation?
Kevin R: I'm nearby, standby to take over if needed. Maya, do we know customer impact yet?
Samir: quick check: 2 customers showing elevated error/latency traces — some 503s from model backend around the same time as spike. Linking trace: https://traces/redwood/trace/0a1b2c
Lia P: customer support reported increased 10s tail latencies for embeddings+generation on two teams. No data exfil or auth issues.
Maya (oncall): paging Kevin to help with routing changes. @Kevin R can we route non-prod traffic to lower priority pool and force-model-fallback for prod?
Kevin R: after looking, the primary model pool hit a KV cache churn from a large prefix-heavy workload. Quick mitigation: flip fallback routing for /v1/generate to model:small-quant for 10m, exclude internal batch job IPs. Running command now: 
```bash
redwoodctl route update --route /v1/generate --fallback model:small-quant --duration 10m
```
obs-bot: Route update accepted. New routing in effect across us-east-1 in ~30s.
Maya (oncall): checking dashboard — latency 95p dropping from 9.8s -> 2.1s after fallback. Burn rate for the endpoint down to 1.05x on 5m window.
Samir: confirming error rates down too. It looks like a short-lived KV-cache cold start from a periodic ML workload that spiked keys. Might be noise from internal batch job hitting the same model.
Lia P: ops note — we saw a single large internal batch job start around the same time (job id job-7721). Should we exclude internal-job traffic from SLO calculation?
Kevin R: yes, we should. Right now our burnrate alert is routing-agnostic and counts everything. Excluding internal service accounts or IP ranges from SLO eval will reduce noise.
Maya (oncall): agreed. After we stabilize, we should tune the alert to avoid paging for short sharp spikes and internal-triggered load.
obs-bot: Incident INC-2023-8492: mitigated by routing fallback at 1764501234. Resolution state: degraded->partial.
Maya (oncall): moving thread to post-incident tuning. TL;DR: quick fallback mitigated customer impact. Root cause hypothesis: internal batch job caused KV cache churn and temporary burn in token processing.
Kevin R: proposed alert changes: 1) require cross-window correlation: only page when both 5m and 1h windows are over thresholds (reduces pages from ephemeral spikes). 2) add min_request_count to rule so low-volume endpoints don't page. 3) exclude internal service accounts and healthchecks from SLO metrics. 4) add a 10m for: clause to avoid immediate flapping paging.
Samir: +1. Also add a multi-window aggregation tweak: use max_over_time on 5m and avg_over_time on 1h to reduce sensitivity to short bursts.
Maya (oncall): can someone draft the alert rule YAML? We'll iterate and push to staging.
Kevin R: Draft inlined rule — please review:
```yaml
# alerting rule draft: slo burnrate (route-level, exclude internal)
groups:
  - name: slo-burnrate.rules
    rules:
      - alert: SLOBurnRateHighRoute
        expr: |
          (
            max_over_time(slo_burn_rate{route="/v1/generate",env!="internal"}[5m]) > 3
            and
            avg_over_time(slo_burn_rate{route="/v1/generate",env!="internal"}[1h]) > 1.2
          )
        for: 10m
        labels:
          severity: page
        annotations:
          summary: "SLO burn rate high for /v1/generate (multi-window)"
          runbook: https://confluence.internal/runbooks/slo-burn
          pager: paging-policy:page-on-high
```
Lia P: looks good. For paging label we should only page for severity:page if route impacts production customers (prod=true label) and request_count>100 in 1h.
Samir: add suggestion to compute request_count and incorporate into expr: e.g., `and increase_over_time(requests_total{route="/v1/generate"}[1h]) > 100`.
Maya (oncall): agreed — want the final to be strict enough to avoid noise but still catch real regressions. Let's capture follow-ups: create a post-incident ticket with actions: update rule, create new dashboard panel for internal-job traffic by service-account, add exclusion filter in SLO pipeline, and update runbook to include model-fallback step.
Kevin R: filing JIRA: INFR-4567 - "Tune slo burnrate alert + exclude internal jobs" and linking INC-2023-8492. I'll attach draft rule and request review from observability.
obs-bot: JIRA INFR-4567 created: https://jira.internal/browse/INFR-4567
Maya (oncall): owners: Kevin R (alert), Samir (root cause follow-up), Lia P (customer comms & dashboard). ETA: alert change in staging by EOD, production after 48h review.
Samir: follow-up item — batch job owners (team-batch) should throttle or use dedicated model pool. I'll ping them.
Kevin R: will add tests in staging to simulate a short 5m spike vs sustained 1h burn to validate we only page on sustained events. Also will add unit to ensure healthchecks/internal tags are excluded.
Lia P: for support: I'll draft a short customer-facing summary and note in the incident timeline.
Maya (oncall): final notes: adjust pager policy: set page-backoff to 30m for same-route repeat pages to avoid multiple wake-ups during anomalous hour. Also add a health dashboard alert: show internal vs external traffic on the SLO dashboard.
Samir: sounds good. Anything else?
Kevin R: one more operational tweak — add a grafana panel with a small script widget linking to quick mitigation commands (redwoodctl route update...) for oncall runbook. That will speed next mitigation.
Maya (oncall): perfect. I'll close incident thread in 1hr after docs + JIRA updates. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
